method: All12 exact final captures were physically opened with view_image at original detail after TurnHub replacement/feed lift; all3 original sketch PNGs and native TurnHub-v1 were physically opened. Hashes below bind that inspection to exact files. No Unity interaction, source changes or image edits performed by reviewer.
scope: Six12-cell pose sheets (rest/turn90/max-recoil at1920x1080 and1024x768), six9-cell definition sheets covering54definitions. Source style comparisons are visual; numerical contact/sweep/test results belong to separate root validation.

observations: Standalone ivory/navy cylindrical hub with dense ballpoint hatching and circular lip.
No wide disk plane or cream rectangle attached below its foot.

overallFindings: Common warm ivory/navy pen-drawn material language now connects bases, weapons, ink accessories and buildings.
Old support-crop cream rectangle is absent from the inspected final assemblies.
No obvious detached primary weapon heads, missing corners or panel clipping in these12static captures.
Residual differences remain in foundation proportions, slow-field height, small-scale readability and some brass/texture density; this is not a claim of100percent sketch fidelity.

observations: Seven weapon families remain identifiable: barrel bundle, pen nib, open mortar, five-nib fan, star disc, two stapler jaws and porous sponge.
New navy/ivory turn hub sits on the left disk; old cream rectangle from the support crop is absent.
Barricade wood/armor, workshop wrench roof/tools, generator glass/flywheel and blue grille field share the pen-drawn material vocabulary.
Three battery weapons occupy distinct seats; no obvious floating heads or cut-off contours at this capture scale.
residuals: Standard base remains a broad regular tiled platform with a relatively small single weapon, compared with compact chipped masonry in01.
Slow field is a taller multi-tier assembly than the low ring in03.
Fine small accessories are much less prominent than the primary weapon silhouettes.
